title: Molise: Diesel Prices Pull Ahead of the National Average
dek: Self-service Gasolio in Molise has climbed for six straight days, even as Benzina holds a fraction below what the rest of Italy is paying.
body: Molise's self-service prices tell a split story today: Benzina averages €2.0105 per liter, about 0.7 cents below the national self-service average of €2.0172, while Gasolio sits at €2.1629, roughly 1.3 cents above the €2.1502 national mark. Diesel drivers in Molise are now paying a premium relative to the rest of the country, even as the region's petrol stays a touch cheaper than average.

The direction of travel has been steadily upward for both fuels over the past week. Self-service Gasolio rose from €2.1326 to €2.1629 — up about 1.4% — with much of that increase landing in a sharp jump between August 18 and August 20. Benzina climbed more gently over the same stretch, from €1.9986 to €2.0105, up roughly 0.6%. Of Molise's 175 registered stations, 153 reported prices today, up from 151 the day before — an 87% reporting rate that points to a small but consistently active regional network.

Producing a grounded, numbers-first write-up like this for a different one of Italy's 20 regions every single morning — checking day-over-day moves, national comparisons, and station counts before anyone's had coffee — isn't something a manually maintained spreadsheet could keep pace with. Fuel Dashboard rebuilds itself automatically each day, pulling the latest MIMIT data and regenerating the charts and this article without anyone opening Excel. It's built and maintained entirely with Claude Code.
